cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Merciful Lie
cards.instruction: Choose a truth your character believes would hurt someone. Keep it from them, even as honesty becomes harder.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's use what I taught you. The magazine hasn't rejected your poem. They think it deserves its own booklet.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They returned it. If even you think it's hopeless, I'll stop writing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're nearly doing it my way. That's why they returned it. They can't give it enough space.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Will you write that on the cover? With your name?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Gladly. 'A voice that deserves more space.' Print my name large enough for the editor to see.

mechanism: A shields a former writing pupil from rejection by claiming its teaching produced work beyond the editor capacity, then stakes its own name on that claim.
confusable: Not simple praise: B threatened withdrawal makes the concealment protective and later requires a concrete endorsement.
comparison: Interception of painful bakery feedback versus public commitment to a comforting explanation.
seedUse: Keep D15 returned poem/stop-writing/cover request; S05 teacher credit becomes a way to offer the lie sincerely.
